analysis.investment_thesis: JSLL is a genuinely excellent business — 31% ROIC, 47% revenue CAGR, 40% operating margins — but the Magic Formula demands both quality AND cheapness, and at a ~1.6% earnings yield (EBIT ₹141 Cr / EV ~₹8,612 Cr), the price completely negates the business quality. The market has already fully priced in years of exceptional growth, leaving no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Exceptional ROIC ~31% (EBIT ₹141 Cr / Invested Capital ~₹460 Cr), far above the 25% 'excellent' threshold
Revenue CAGR 47.2% and operating income CAGR 98.6% over 3 years — rare operational momentum
Asset-light Ayurvedic/clinic model driving 40% operating margins and 91% gross margins with low debt (D/E 0.30)
key_risks: Earnings yield ~1.6% (EBIT ₹141 Cr / EV ~₹8,612 Cr) — needs to be >12% for Magic Formula; company must grow earnings 8x just to reach fair value
Borrowings surged from ₹1 Cr to ₹106 Cr in FY2025 alongside capex of ₹42 Cr — expansion may dilute returns if not executed well
Ayurvedic healthcare is regulatory/reputational risk-heavy; business model sustainability at scale is unproven beyond the Shuddhi brand
red_flags: P/E 64x, P/B 24x, EV/EBITDA 29x — all screaming overvaluation on Magic Formula metrics
FCF only ₹27 Cr vs Market Cap ₹8,530 Cr — FCF yield is 0.3%, essentially zero
Finance costs jumped from ₹0 to ₹11 Cr with ₹106 Cr in new borrowings in FY2025 — leverage inflecting upward
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula verdict is swift: JSLL scores in the top decile on Return on Capital (~31%) but in the bottom decile on Earnings Yield (~1.6%). EBIT of ₹141 Cr against an enterprise value of roughly ₹8,612 Cr (Market Cap ₹8,530 + Borrowings ₹106 - Cash ₹24) produces an earnings yield that is roughly 7-8x below my minimum threshold of 12%. The P/E of 64x and EV/EBITDA of 29x confirm the market has priced in perfection. Even granting a generous 30% forward EBIT growth, the earnings yield only reaches ~2.1% — still deeply unattractive.

The business itself is hard not to admire. Operating margins of 40%+ in healthcare with a near-zero debt model until FY2025 is exceptional execution. The Shuddhi brand Ayurveda clinics are building network effects and the 98.6% operating income CAGR shows real operating leverage. But the Magic Formula teaches one lesson above all others: even the best business destroys wealth when purchased at the wrong price. At 24x book and a sub-2% earnings yield, this is priced for a decade of flawless execution with zero room for error. I'd revisit if the price dropped 60-70% — but not today.
